question: A student had 73 pages. They removed 7. They multiplied by 9. They multiplied by 7. They multiplied by 7 again. They noted a distractor page. How many pages total?
A school had 136 students. They doubled. They added 23. They removed 173. They added 33. They added 59 final registrations. How many students enroll?
A team scored 122 points. They added 52. They added 14. They tripled for the tournament. They added 23 bonus points. How many points did they score?
A store had 63 items. They removed 1. They multiplied by 6. They removed 219. They added 13. They doubled. How many items in stock?

A student studied 128 pages. By morning, they added 21. By afternoon, they added 45. By evening, they added 3. By night, they added 40. By next morning, they added 67. By noon, they added 64. How many pages studied?
A team scored 71 points. In Q1, they added 7. In Q2, they added 74. In Q3, they added 5. In Q4, they tripled. How many total points?
A student started with 23 pages. They added 44. They multiplied by 7. They multiplied by 4. They added 15. They noted a distractor task. How many pages total?
A factory produced 78 units. They multiplied by 7. They multiplied by 9. They multiplied by 2. They added 64. They noted a distractor batch of 15 units. How many units?
Two players combined 113 points. Player A removed 92. Player A removed 4 more. Player A removed 8 final points. Player A added 73. Player A removed 13. How many points does Player A have?
Two friends met with 177 marbles. In the morning, they added 22. By afternoon, they removed 67. By evening, they added 80. By night, they added 63. How many marbles do they have (as a measure)?
A factory started with 216 units. They removed 148. They added 4. They divided by 6. They divided by 3. How many units per location?

A student had 76 assignments. In the morning, they added 4. By noon, they removed 62. By afternoon, they multiplied by 5. By evening, they removed 11. By night, they added 14. By final, they multiplied by 7. How many assignments?
A player had 85 chips. They removed 32. They added 69. They added 55. They multiplied by 7. They removed 999. How many chips remain?
A company started with 218 employees. In Q1, they added 30. They multiplied by 5. They removed 1,152 (due to restructuring). They multiplied by 6. They multiplied by 4. How many employees?
Two players combined 137 tokens. They added 19. They divided by 4. They added 26. They added 4. They added 31. How many tokens per player (as a measure)?
A store started with 61 items. They removed 43. They added 74. They added 26. They removed 104. They added 38. They multiplied by 9. How many items (as a word quantity)?
A bakery started with 47 pastries. They multiplied by 7. They added 22. They added 53. They multiplied by 9. How many pastries were baked?

A student started with 18 pages. Morning: they doubled. By afternoon, they removed 62. By evening, they removed 1. By night, they removed 4. By next day, they removed 3. By next night, they removed 1 final page. How many pages remain?

Maria started with 56 cookies to sell. She dropped 5 cookies and had to discard them. Each remaining batch was placed into 8 equal boxes. Then 51 more cookies arrived. Her friend had baked 12 brownies as well. The total cookies were then needed 7 times for a week-long event. How many cookies will be required in total?

A merchant had 67 items to sell. He removed 26 damaged items from stock. Then he ordered a bulk shipment—8 containers arriving with multiple items. Each container held the same amount, and he had 41 items pre-packed. Finally, 33 gift items were added to the inventory. How many items does the merchant have for sale?

A coach's team equipment started at 101 items. He added 44 new uniforms in the morning. By afternoon, 68 items needed repair and were removed from play. Training added back 41 items. Then 95 damaged items were discarded. The next day, 17 more items were removed for maintenance. How many items remain ready for use?

An athlete started training with 39 daily exercise reps. She increased to 27 more reps. The next session, she reduced by 14 reps. In evening practice, she added 42 reps. By the end of the day, she reduced her final total by 59 reps. What was the total number of reps completed at day's end?

A bakery made 211 loaves in the morning. By midday, they added 43 more. They doubled production for the afternoon shift—5 times the morning amount. That evening, they divided the total output in half for packaging. Each package was ordered 7 times over. How many packaged units were ordered?

Rachel and her brother compared collections. Rachel started with 155 cards. She gave away 114 cards to her brother. She then organized them—4 cards per page, multiplied 3 times over for display, then again multiplied by 9 for a large exhibition. Finally, she lost 1229 rare cards in a move. Her brother had half that amount. How many cards does Rachel have after the move?

A store manager tracked inventory. He began with 179 units. He removed 96 units for a clearance sale. He ordered a bulk shipment—7 times the removed amount. Then he subtracted 54 defective units. He multiplied the remaining stock by 4 for a mega-order. Then 55 units arrived as a surprise delivery. His assistant was comparing this to another location's stock. How many units are in the final inventory?
